Preserve the corrected baseline’s exact loss as an explicit control; change supervision separately from architecture, optimizer, sampling, and loss normalization. BERT4Rec requires masked-target training with bidirectional context and appended-mask inference; prevent target leakage. The [original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) establishes this setup, while a [replicability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483) shows that implementation and convergence time materially affect comparisons. For this benchmark, use one model/category, fixed splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and identical evaluation candidates. Recommended reporting: masking policy, actual supervised targets/update and total targets, updates, completed epochs, GPU-seconds, hardware, and validation overhead. Compare within equal GPU-time allocations under the 200-epoch/200-batch caps; equal epochs alone need not equalize supervision or compute. Charge failed trials and diagnostics to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

For each dataset, retain paired binary hit indicators for the same 200 users. Report ΔHR@10=(candidate-only hits−baseline-only hits)/200, discordant counts, and a paired confidence interval; one net hit changes dataset HR@10 by 0.5 percentage points. Exact McNemar testing uses discordant pairs ([NIST](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman1/auxillar/mcnemar.htm)). For the four-dataset macro difference, bootstrap user pairs within each dataset, then average dataset differences equally. These intervals reflect user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; they do not estimate training-seed variability.

Predeclare a small comparison set, equal tuning allocations, and selection rules; disclose every validation query. Repeated optimization can overfit the selection criterion ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Adjust prespecified multiple comparisons, but ordinary paired tests or bootstraps do not remove adaptive selection bias. Treat reused-validation gains as exploratory; freeze the final choice before the host’s held-out evaluation.
